chunks: Ahmad ibn Mihran, from the one who narrates it, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Huzayfa ibn Mansur, who said:
I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'My uncle swept the Ka'bah and took from its soil, so we heal with it.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Return it to it.'

key_terms.الْكَعْبَة: The Ka'bah, the cubic building in Mecca

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on taking soil from the Ka'bah for healing?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the status of the Ka'bah's soil by instructing that it be returned to its place, thereby distinguishing between mere possession for healing and the act of removing it from the sacred precincts. This ruling underscores the principle of *Ihtiram* (reverence) for the physical structure of the House of God, a key concept in Shia jurisprudence regarding the sanctity of the Ka'bah's components.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Mihran, from the one who narrates it, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Huzeyfa Bin Mansour who said,
‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that my uncle is a sweeper of the Kabah and took from its soil. So we tend to heal by it. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Return it back to it’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ahmad ibn Mehran has narrated from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Hudhayfah ibn Mansur who has said the following:
“I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, that my uncle once swept al-Ka‘bah and took of the dust and we use it as medicine. He (the Imam) said, ‘You must return it back.’”
